ratings_why.fun: Earns 8 over 7 because the board's shape is the decision: deep chains make Hop Bine, Kissing Bough and Missel grow per level, wide trees survive deaths, and Bloom flips which host size you want. You re-solve that every turn.
ratings_why.distinct: Hosts and vines that turn other tribes' growth into your own play unlike any tribe today, though 'copy what another unit gains' is a familiar idea from other games.

verdict_why: The engine is in a great spot. Two rules don't read clearly yet (Mistletoe's net gain, and whether a Dodder falls when its enemy host dies), and both are worth one more pass.

points.text: Mistletoe Clump: is it +1/+1 in total, or +1/+1 plus the 1/1 it takes? And does what it takes count as a gain that its own climbers copy? Say the net amount.

When Cousin Dodder's or Dodder Thread's enemy host dies, does the Dodder 'fall', so Old Man's Beard gives it a third of the dead enemy? Falling says 'your board', so state it either way. If yes, it's a lovely kill-and-feast combo.
Viscum buffs every friendly unit, and climbers also copy their host's buff, so deep chains double-dip down every level. Keep it, and list it under Johnny tricks so players find it.

Kissing Bough must be played next to the root, so the board needs a free slot beside the root late in the game. That placement puzzle is good; Visiting Card could also say it works as a set-up for the Bough.
Chain depth against tree width is the tribe's best hidden decision. Name it in 'plays' next to big host against small host, so the drafting choice is visible.

standouts.why: Lady Hedera re-hosts every turn and drags her whole chain onto the biggest unit: a self-steering engine that rewards building under her.
Cousin Dodder climbs the enemy, steals, and jumps again after each kill; with Lattice Ivy under it, the whole branch feeds on the opponent.
Traveller's Joy regroups the tree, and each mover's +2/+2 is itself a gain that cascades down to its climbers.

weakest.why: Barley-sugar Twiner is a plain Start of Combat buff; it does nothing the core keyword doesn't already do better.
Lattice Ivy goes dead once Lady Hedera is down, since she gives every climber the full share.
Ivy Sprig is a fine opener but carries no hook into any later build.

flags.note: Net gain and whether the taken stats copy down to its climbers aren't stated.
Doesn't say whether a Dodder losing its enemy host counts as falling.
Missel's buff grows with the climber count, and each climber copies it, so it's roughly quadratic in climbers (bounded by 7 slots).
A golden Hanger-on on a crowded host pays 4 gold a turn from Tier 2.
Two golden Hederas chained double her copy twice (x4 down the chain): finite, but a big high roll.
